items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I thought somewhere along the line a wrote a lot of pop songs and I thought maybe there was a chance along the way there was going to be some pop music in my future, of performing my own songs and being Billy Joel or James Taylor.

ctx.x: Did you get to a point on a particular day or time when you said you know I’m going to make my living doing this?

You know I never did. The only thing that I wanted to do I thought was to — I thought somewhere along the line a wrote a lot of pop songs and I thought maybe there was a chance along the way there was going to be some pop music in my future, of performing my own songs and being Billy Joel or James Taylor. And it’s interesting you should ask that question because I never ever realized that I was making a living doing what I was — and I was playing with my dad, and I’d be getting these $600 checks and $1000 checks…
What was your repertoire at the time? CCR and that kind of stuff?

items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: probably ’83 like the day after Christmas Billy Joel was at Brendan Byrne arena also

ctx.x: But I think it’s actually a number of things. I mean when I was a kid I loved comedy records. I had Bill Cosby’s “Why is There Air?” I don’t know how that record got in the house but I learned all the bits and I liked George Carlin after that, I had all — three or

four — three of his records. And I liked to watch Johnny Carson and I liked the timing of a story, of a joke. And I always point to, I don’t know if I mentioned this the first time or not, there were three concerts in ’85 — March 14th of ’85 Sinatra was at the Brendan Byrne arena in New Jersey. And then that summer Springsteen was at the big stadium, and previously about a year or two earlier, probably ’83 like the day after Christmas Billy Joel was at Brendan Byrne arena also. And I loved the way it was not…

road — and those tours were like six weeks because we have the itinerary on our wall in the house of my mother’s mother and father stayed with us and they went all over the place. That’s 1972. And so the fact that there’s a film of that is so exciting, and to watch them joking around and Benny goes, “Well play another one” and Zoot says, “No, I’m not going to play another one.” And it’s really — it was sort of inside baseball you know but it was so — it’s just wonderful to see that there was some joy out there.
